title: CI fails when an evaluation does more work than its budget
what: A test group holds two evaluations to step budgets: a cold run (206,834 steps, budget 227,000) and a re-run after editing a literal nothing reads (378, budget 420, and under 5% of the cold run).
changes: No. The trampoline now returns the step count it already kept, and a new entry point, called only by the test, runs the same trampoline.
mechanism: Evaluator.evaluate_counting_work runs the trampoline through run_slice(~step_budget=max_int) and returns the count; Trampoline.Yielding.SliceDone carries the total. The only other matches on SliceDone ignore the new field. No global state.
argument: No production path changes what it computes: the new entry point is used by the test alone, and both trampoline drivers interpret Bind, Next and Done the same way.
assumes: That step counts repeat exactly across runs (the PR says so; not re-checked here).
risk: Budgets have about 10% headroom and a count more than 25% under fails too, so harmless refactors will need budget bumps: noise, not flakiness. Not counted: the reuse pre-pass, statics, the worker's streaming path.
tests_have: Both runs check their values (6085 and 7085), so a stale reuse in the re-run would fail.
tests_missing: Edit a literal that is read (fib(10) to fib(11)) and check the value equals a fresh run's: the guard against reusing too much.
Check the re-run's step count and probe samples equal a fresh run's.
Check the counted path's value equals Evaluator.evaluate's.

title: Test: statics analyzes each expression within a budget
what: hazel analyze --count-passes counts how often statics analyzes each expression; a test pins the known multipliers (a recursive let 3x, nested recursive lets 27x, ...) and budgets every corpus program (at most 5 analyses of one expression, 2.5 on average).
changes: Its own commits: no (a counter that is off unless the CLI flag sets it). It is stacked on #2603 and #2651, which do change statics.
mechanism: A check at the top of uexp_to_info_map reads a ref that is None unless the flag sets it; the counts go in a table keyed by expression id.
argument: With the flag off, the only new work is reading one ref per call; nothing statics computes changes.
assumes: Merged after #2603 and #2651, as it says: its diff includes their code.
risk: A pass count cannot see a wrong type: the new test throws the info map away. With the flag on, Exp.rep_id could raise on an expression without ids (CLI only).
tests_have: The tests carried from #2603 check results: Test_CtxIndex compares indexed lookups with a plain scan; Test_Statics_Let checks nested lets type-check consistently.
tests_missing: Assert each pinned case's type and that it has no errors, since statics already runs there.
Keep an expected top-level type and error list per corpus program, and compare: where #2603's analyze-once could silently change a type.

title: Test: a re-run beside a library with recursive members stays within its step budget
what: A third step-budget case: a library module with recursive members, and an edit to a knob only the last line reads; the re-run takes 132 steps (budget 145, under 5% of the cold run's 127,394).
changes: Its own commit: no (test only). It is stacked on #2678 and #2675; #2675 changes which expressions are reused.
argument: No non-test code of its own.
risk: 13 steps of headroom; the low-side check fails below 109.
tests_missing: The other direction for #2675: edit inside the library (range(300) to range(301), expect 45458) and inside a recursive member's body, each checked against a fresh run.

title: Test: what the eval worker sends and gets back stays within a byte budget
what: Measures the encoded size of the eval worker's request and answer for two programs, with budgets about 10% over today (probes.hz: 25,180 and 3,617 bytes; B2T2 leftjoin: 60,628 and 21,258).
changes: Its own commit: no (test only). It is stacked on #2606 and #2608, which change runtime behaviour.
mechanism: Test only: it repeats the worker's resolve, evaluate and keep sequence itself.
argument: No non-test code of its own.
risk: It never looks at the answer's value: a broken evaluation shows only if the answer shrinks by more than 25%. Native and js_of_ocaml Marshal sizes not compared.
tests_have: The carried Test_WorkerServer (#2606) compares a run with the held cache against a fresh run, on a small program.
tests_missing: Decode the request and answer and check they round-trip.
Compare the answer's value with Evaluator.evaluate on the same elaboration, and the second answer's value with the first's.
head: 35edf2d1d8

title: SPIKE: compile the Hazel evaluator with wasm_of_ocaml and benchmark it
what: A draft spike, not meant to merge: it benchmarks the evaluator compiled with wasm_of_ocaml. To build, it splits util, swaps the statics memo, and removes the builtin livelits; it also commits 957 build artifacts under _build-wasm/.
changes: Yes, as it stands: the builtin livelits (^slider, ^emotion) no longer type or elaborate, and three livelit tests are deleted.
mechanism: Builtins.ctx_entries drops the builtin livelits; Statics.mk's memo empties the whole table at 1,000 entries instead of evicting least-recently-used ones (keys still compared structurally, so a cost change, not a result change).
argument: Not a merge candidate. Its benchmark compares the two backends' results by a hash of each workload's printed result (three workloads matched); that is a spot check, not a test.
assumes: That it is never merged as it is.
risk: If merged: the livelit regression, the deleted tests, 957 build artifacts in history, and a dune 3.17 requirement.
tests_missing: Before wasm is used for real: a CI check that results match across the two backends. Keep the util split, if wanted, as a fresh PR without the artifacts or the livelit removal.
head: a7b5559cbb
